_about: The lexicon key (`harness lexicon lookup`, keying_spec.md §2.15): how a ratified native form is addressed in ASCII. Read whole by harness/marks.py `handle_table`, through layout.shared: a text holding its own config/handle.json replaces this one, since two key schemes share ASCII characters with different meanings and neither can inherit from the other. This is the Jesup Americanist notation's, The Chukchee's, moved verbatim out of marks.HANDLE_MARKERS on 2026-11-16.
_injective: One marker per mark class, and the classes collide on purpose: `^` serves the superscripts and the caron/circumflex, `.` both dots. A collision yields two distinct forms with one key, which lookup refuses as a key collision and names both, so inventing a marker against a case the corpus does not attest would be guesswork ahead of an instance.
_passthrough: Every ASCII character passes through as itself: the ASCII policy makes U+0027 and U+002D load-bearing inside Tier-1, and the bases of every marked sort are ASCII letters after NFD.
_tokens: A combining mark contributes only its marker: after NFD its base is already an ASCII letter and has passed through. An atomic letter contributes an ASCII base and a marker; ˊ and ˙ are marks that stand alone and so contribute no base.
